summary.text: The Royal Road was an ancient highway that the Achaemenid Empire reorganized and rebuilt for trade in the 5th century BCE.
It was built for rapid communication across the western empire from Susa to Sardis, and was probably perfected under Darius I.
Mounted couriers were supposed to cover about 2,699 km in nine days, a trip that took ninety days on foot.

facts.label: Courier time
facts.value: Nine days on horseback, ninety on foot

facts.label: Improved by
facts.value: Darius I, who turned existing roads into one

items.prompt: A message has to cross a vast empire in days, not months. What system made that possible on this road?

options.label: A lone rider crossing the whole route
Relays of riders at stations with fresh horses
Signal fires lit along the route
Carrier pigeons housed at each station

items.explain: The road included posting stations with fresh horses and relays of swift mounted messengers.

items.prompt: On foot the trip took ninety days; mounted couriers were meant to do it in nine. About how much faster is that?

options.label: About twice as fast
About five times as fast
About ten times as fast
About thirty times as fast

items.explain: Ninety days divided by nine is ten, so the couriers were meant to be about ten times faster than a walker.

items.prompt: Why do archaeologists suspect the westernmost sections were first built by Assyrian kings?

options.label: The road ran through their old empire and not by the easiest route
Herodotus named an Assyrian king as the builder
Assyrian coins were found at each station
Darius I wrote that he copied Assyria

items.explain: The road followed neither the shortest nor the easiest route between the empire's key cities, and it plunges through the heart of the old Assyrian empire.

items.prompt: Why are the eastern segments in present-day northern Iran missing from Herodotus's account?

options.label: The road did not exist there until Roman times
He was forbidden to travel east
Those stretches were built after he died
He wrote from the viewpoint of a Greek in the West

items.explain: Herodotus did not note the eastern segments because his view of Persia was that of an Ionian Greek in the West.

items.prompt: Darius I is linked with the Royal Road. What did he actually do?

options.label: Built every mile from scratch
Rebuilt it with Roman-style gravel
Improved existing roads and joined them into one post road
Moved it to follow the shortest route

items.explain: Darius I improved the existing road network into the Royal Road, connecting the parts into a unified whole, primarily as a post road.

items.prompt: Stretches across the central plateau of Iran, like the Great Khorasan Road, share the route of which famous trade network?

options.label: The Silk Road
The Amber Road
The Incense Route
The Appian Way

items.explain: Stretches of the Royal Road across the central plateau of Iran coincide with the major trade route known as the Silk Road.
